A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OpenVLThinker work, and their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison. Part of an example overflows v3 page 27, but its full text remains extractable, allowing comparison with v2.

before.justification: V2 reports original benchmark evaluations, training ablations, reasoning analyses and ConTextual experiments, including results explicitly evaluated by the authors.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds benchmark evaluations, training controls and caption-quality experiments.

M1.justification: The proposed iterative SFT-GRPO procedure, curriculum, filtering and base-model restart rule remain unchanged. Restarting was already specified in v2 Section 4.2. V3 evaluates alternative training and captioning configurations without establishing a revision to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds evaluation on MM-Star and WeMath, extending the existing perception and visual reasoning coverage with additional benchmark data. The EMMA category results disaggregate an existing benchmark; the original six benchmarks and ConTextual study remain.

E2.justification: V3 adds substantive methodological controls: continued training versus restarting in Table 5, and SFT-only and RL-only comparators in the shared-data comparison of Table 9. These expand comparison beyond the retained external-model and training-stage comparisons. The new benchmark tables reuse Qwen2.5-VL and VLAA-Thinker.

E3.justification: New experimental designs compare restarting with continued training, single-stage training on a nominally shared 12K dataset with convergence and validation-based checkpoint selection, and 3B versus 7B captioners under k=4 rejection sampling. These substantially expand the controls; the original evaluation metrics and inference settings are retained.

E4.justification: V3 adds tests of whether restarting helps generalization, whether iterative training outperforms SFT-only or RL-only training, and how initial caption quality affects successive training stages (Tables 5, 9 and 10). The earlier filtering, curriculum, reasoning-length and caption-feedback analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation-run seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. V3 continues reporting single-valued results. Its new k=4 settings concern candidate sampling rather than uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: V3 adds substantial results across benchmarks and ablations. Table 7 reports OpenVLThinker scores of 61.9 on MM-Star and 64.1 on WeMath; Table 6 shows it trailing both comparators on EMMA-Code despite leading the other categories. Original main results remain unchanged. New OpenVLThinker scores in Tables 5 and 9 differ from Table 1 without reconciled settings, so they do not establish same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, SFT and RL objectives, GRPO equation and curriculum construction are unchanged apart from formatting. V3 adds empirical rationale rather than new formal assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about iterative SFT-RL, reasoning actions, data efficiency and six-benchmark improvements. The added experiments support existing contributions without redefining their stated scope.

C2.justification: V3 adds explanations linking restarting to reduced overfitting and error accumulation, stronger initial captions to better subsequent training, and preliminary stages to faster hard-stage convergence. Appendix A.3 attributes its results to iteration beyond merely combining SFT and RL, although its controls do not directly isolate that distinction. Existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 adds an eight-H100 node specification, approximate per-stage GPU costs, baseline training costs and filtering/checkpoint-selection details. Existing hyperparameters and access links remain. The new timing estimates are not reconciled with the retained Appendix C statement of 30-minute SFT and 20-hour RL stages per iteration.

R1.justification: V3 adds references for MM-Star and WeMath and expands its explanation of restarting through previously cited self-training work. All 89 earlier references are retained; the main related-work positioning and novelty claims remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 adds a restart-analysis passage, acknowledgments and an Additional Experiments appendix with four subsections. Earlier Appendices A-C become B-D with updated cross-references. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: New Tables 5-10 substantially expand the tabular presentation of controls, benchmark results and computational costs. Existing appendix displays are renumbered or repositioned. The rearrangement pushes part of the derivative reasoning example below v3 page 27, clipping content that was fully visible on v2 page 24.

improvement.justification: The added benchmarks and controls address useful evidential gaps, but their benefit is weakened by unexplained score differences across Tables 1, 5 and 9 and unreconciled compute accounting in Table 8, Appendix A.3 and Appendix C. The new layout also clips a previously readable example. Because the reporting ambiguities affect evidence for iteration and efficiency, the gains cannot be reliably weighed against the loss of consistency and readability.
